verdict: Simulated outcome under stated assumptions: StudyFlow takes a median share of 0.18 (p10 0.16, p90 0.19). Biggest threat: Free Planner responds with adding a feature (share 0.190 -> 0.140 (-0.050, -26.3%)). Fragility 0.09, confidence high.
who_buys: Power planners: 33 of 90 simulated agents chose StudyFlow (0.37)
Budget-conscious students: 22 of 120 simulated agents chose StudyFlow (0.18)
who_rejects: Free-tool loyalists: 0 of 90 simulated agents chose StudyFlow (0.00); most chose Free Planner

risks.title: Free Planner responds with adding a feature
risks.evidence: Competitor Strategist: the rival's best one-step response among the bounded moves.

risks.title: Willingness to pay is lower than assumed
risks.evidence: Devil's Advocate: if willingness to pay (budget) is 20% lower than assumed, the simulated share changes as shown.

risks.title: Customers are more price-sensitive than assumed
risks.evidence: Devil's Advocate: if price sensitivity is 20% higher than assumed, the simulated share changes as shown.

experiments.title: Free-tier landing variant against Free Planner
experiments.hypothesis: A free tier with a paid AI upgrade keeps StudyFlow attractive when Free Planner reacts with a price cut, a new feature or a promotion.
experiments.pass_threshold: Proposed test threshold (not an established benchmark): free-tier sign-ups are at least 15% of 100+ visitors and at least 10% of them try the paid upgrade page.

experiments.title: Two-price landing page (S$9 vs S$7.20)
experiments.hypothesis: Students who want AI planning will join a paid waitlist for StudyFlow at S$9, not only at S$7.20.
experiments.pass_threshold: Proposed test threshold (not an established benchmark): waitlist sign-up rate at S$9 is at least 8% of 100+ unique visitors and at least 70% of the rate at S$7.20.

experiments.title: Price-ladder survey with target students
experiments.hypothesis: Target students rate S$9 a month as acceptable for an AI study planner.
experiments.pass_threshold: Proposed test threshold (not an established benchmark): at least 40% of 50+ respondents in the target segment place S$9 at or below their "getting expensive" price.

limitations: Simulated outcome under stated assumptions; not a forecast of real sales.
